rationale: A legitimate but incremental recombination of two already-tested components (fractional under-depreciation carrier × FFO-deficit conditioner) whose signs are internally consistent and whose invariance argument (ib+dp is first-order independent of the depreciation choice) is correct, though the dp denominator remains a fat-tailed, low-dp-firm hazard that 1% winsorization only partly tames.

The two ingredients improved different parts of the evidence in the archive (IND_ADJ deviation lifted the slope, MIN(dvt,sstk) lifted alpha t and Sharpe), the signs compose coherently, and the argument that demeaning a mean-zero deviation avoids the capital-intensity sorting that killed the peer-level version is economically sound.

MA3−MA5 is a smoothed, weakly novel restatement of the already-tested five-year TREND carrier paired with a tested modulator, so it is internally consistent and cheap to run but is close to a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

Sign-consistent and a genuinely untested cross-family cell, but TS_SUM(sstk,3) is mechanically dominated by the same issuance decisions as the already-tested contemporaneous sstk modulator, so the incremental information is likely small.

The expression algebraically collapses to −dev×(RANK(sstk/at)+RANK(prstkc/at)), so issuance and repurchase enter with the *same* sign as amplifiers rather than as the symmetric opposing states the hypothesis claims — an under-depreciating heavy repurchaser is shorted exactly like an under-depreciating issuer — and the same collapse already applied to the archived TwoSidedGap construction.

A defensible but near-cosmetic permutation of two archived signals (the dvt-truncated carrier and the TS_MIN(dvt,5) rigidity modulator) that additionally introduces a large zero mass point for any firm that skipped a dividend in five years, risking unstable portfolio composition despite nominal coverage; the reasoning's claim about "avoiding re-using the dividend on both sides" is also spurious since the modulator is sstk.
